I have no idea how this behaves when your input to boost::urls::format is a already a boost::urls::url.

We do have a utility function for this exact case though that I suspect we should use instead.
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/ac69e77ea938e8c2a5bd3dad258cdafd9d3182b7/http/utility.hpp#L340

> Probably still best to use the utility function, considering that it's more clear that's the behavior.

Where I'm coming from is - the whole reason I did this cleanup was because I copy/pasted code that used std::format, and was told to use boost::urls::format (reasonable).  I thought if I got rid of the instances of url formatting with std::format, I'd save the next person from making the same mistake I did.

If we mix use of boost::urls::format and appendUrlPieces, we aren't any better off - people will end up copy/pasting boost::urls::format in situations where appendUrlPieces is wanted.  Considering that boost::urls::format works fine, wouldn't we be better off using it uniformly?

> I'd be curious what

My guess is it will try to coerce something after that first http:// into a hostname (properly encoded), and try to coerce everything after that into a path (again, properly encoded).  Why is this particular set of inputs interesting or relevant - all we ever do in bmcweb is encode paths isn't it?

> > Probably still best to use the utility function, considering that it's more clear that's the behavior.
> 
> Where I'm coming from is - the whole reason I did this cleanup was because I copy/pasted code that used std::format, and was told to use boost::urls::format (reasonable).  I thought if I got rid of the instances of url formatting with std::format, I'd save the next person from making the same mistake I did.

All of this is great, and I appreciate you cleaning it up.

> 
> If we mix use of boost::urls::format and appendUrlPieces, we aren't any better off - people will end up copy/pasting boost::urls::format in situations where appendUrlPieces is wanted.  Considering that boost::urls::format works fine, wouldn't we be better off using it uniformly?

It's pretty rare we hit this pattern.  Generally we would not be putting a URL type into a piece of another URL (in fact, this is the only instance I know of).  Normally we'd pass through the variable pieces, possibly in a struct, and reconstruct the string we wanted without using a URI as input.  Obviously that doesn't work in this case.

> 
> > I'd be curious what
> 
> My guess is it will try to coerce something after that first http:// into a hostname (properly encoded), and try to coerce everything after that into a path (again, properly encoded).  Why is this particular set of inputs interesting or relevant - all we ever do in bmcweb is encode paths isn't it?

Wouldn't it be nice if that were all we parsed :).  We do parse full URIs.

FWIW, I really wish there were a fixed type for "URI path" so we could trust it, but I'm not aware there is.

If this isn't a change you want to make, this is fine, I can go fix it.

> in fact, this is the only instance I know of

this was not my finding.

> Wouldn't it be nice if that were all we parsed :). We do parse full URIs.

Ok, but do we format URLs with protocols and hostnames into existing URLs on purpose?  And if we don't, is your point that appendUrlPieces would fail in a better way than boost::urls::format?

> If this isn't a change you want to make, this is fine, I can go fix it.

It isn't that I don't want to make a change.  Rather, it doesn't seem like the ask is trivial, and before doing the work I just want to understand why it is necessary.
